cards.front: What should you know about key point?
cards.back: Your vocabulary choices directly affect your AO6 mark (up to 16 marks). A wide, ambitious vocabulary demonstrates control and precision - but only when used appropriately.

cards.front: What should you know about connotation matters?
cards.back: "Cheap" and "inexpensive" have similar meanings but different connotations. "Cheap" suggests poor quality; "inexpensive" suggests good value. Choose the word with the right emotional shade.

cards.front: What should you know about common repeat offenders?
cards.back: said, went, looked, got, nice, good, thing, something, very, really

cards.front: What should you know about warning?
cards.back: Don't use words you don't fully understand. Misused ambitious vocabulary is worse than correctly used simple vocabulary.

cards.front: What should you know about creative writing register?
cards.back: For narrative and descriptive writing, aim for accessible but varied vocabulary. Too formal feels stiff; too informal feels unpolished.

cards.front: What should you know about examiner's tip?
cards.back: Vocabulary is judged on range AND appropriateness. A wide vocabulary used incorrectly scores lower than a narrower vocabulary used effectively. Quality and precision matter more than quantity.

cards.front: What should you know about vocabulary exam strategy?
cards.back: Vocabulary choices directly affect your AO6 mark (16 marks). The examiner assesses the range and precision of your word choices across your entire response. Before the exam: Build a personal vocabulary bank. Learn 5-10 ambitious words each week, including their meaning, connotations, and an example sentence. Focus on verbs and adjectives — these carry the most impact. During planning: Jot down key ambitious words you want to include.
